subject: ela
intro: This worksheet covers the whole Key Ideas and Details cluster for informational text: asking and answering questions with text evidence (3.RI.A.1), finding the main idea and key details (3.RI.A.2), and describing how events, ideas, or steps are connected by time, sequence, and cause and effect (3.RI.A.3). Items are grouped by standard and get harder toward the end of each group.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A turtle carries its home on its back. Its hard shell protects its soft body from danger.

WHAT protects a turtle's soft body?
items.answer: A turtle's hard shell protects its soft body.

steps: The question asks WHAT protects the turtle.
The passage says its "hard shell protects its soft body."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Owls sleep during the day. They hunt for mice and other small animals at night.

WHEN do owls hunt?

steps: The question asks WHEN owls hunt.
The passage says they "hunt... at night."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone. His invention let people talk to each other over long distances.

WHO invented the telephone?
items.answer: Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone.

steps: The question asks WHO invented it.
The passage says "Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A cheetah's body is made for speed. Its long legs take big steps, and its bendy spine lets it stretch far with each stride, so it can run faster than any other land animal.

HOW is a cheetah able to run so fast?
items.answer: A cheetah runs fast because its long legs take big steps and its bendy spine lets it stretch far with each stride.

steps: The question asks HOW it runs so fast.
The passage says its "long legs take big steps" and its "bendy spine lets it stretch far."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Many years ago, sailors used the North Star to find their way at night. The star always sits above the north, so sailors could look up and know which direction they were heading, even far out at sea.

WHY was the North Star useful to sailors?
items.answer: The North Star was useful because it always sits above the north, so sailors could look up and know which direction they were heading.

steps: The question asks WHY the star helped.
The passage says it "always sits above the north."
So sailors could tell which way they were going.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Dogs use their bodies to show how they feel. A wagging tail can mean a dog is happy. Flat ears can mean a dog is scared. A low growl can warn that a dog is upset.

What is the main idea of this passage?
items.answer: The main idea is that dogs use their bodies to show how they feel.

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about.
The details tell what a tail, ears, and growl show.
The main idea is that dogs use their bodies to show feelings.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The ocean gives us many useful things. It provides fish and other seafood to eat. It offers a path for ships to carry goods. It even helps make the rain that waters our crops.

What is the main idea?
items.answer: The main idea is that the ocean gives us many useful things.

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about.
Each detail names something useful the ocean gives.
The main idea is that the ocean gives us many useful things.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The firehouse is a busy place. Firefighters check their trucks and tools to make sure everything works. They practice putting out pretend fires so they are ready. When a call comes in, they race out to help.

What is the main idea, and name one detail that supports it?
items.answer: The main idea is that the firehouse is a busy place where firefighters stay ready. One supporting detail: they check their trucks and tools to make sure everything works.

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about: a busy firehouse getting ready.
The main idea is that the firehouse is busy and firefighters stay ready.
One detail: they check their trucks and tools.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The Wright brothers never gave up. They built model after model that failed to fly. They studied how birds used their wings to turn. They tested their ideas again and again until, at last, their airplane lifted off the ground.

What is the main idea, and explain why "They studied birds" is only a detail, not the main idea?
items.answer: The main idea is that the Wright brothers never gave up and kept trying until their airplane flew. "They studied birds" is only one thing they did, so it is a detail, not the main idea that covers the whole passage.

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about: their hard work and not giving up.
The main idea covers the whole passage.
"They studied birds" is one small step, so it is a detail, not the main idea.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

Wetlands may look like plain, muddy fields, but they do important work. They soak up floodwater like a giant sponge, protecting nearby towns. They clean dirty water as it passes through. They are also home to birds, frogs, and fish. Wetlands matter far more than they seem to.

What is the main idea, and give two details that support it?
items.answer: The main idea is that wetlands do important work even though they look plain. Two supporting details: they soak up floodwater to protect towns, and they clean dirty water as it passes through.

steps: Ask what the passage is mostly about: the important work of wetlands.
The main idea covers the whole passage.
Two details: soaking up floodwater and cleaning dirty water.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

First, dark clouds rolled in. Then the rain began to fall. So the game was stopped.

WHY was the game stopped?
items.answer: The game was stopped because the rain began to fall.

steps: The word "So" shows the cause.
The rain "began to fall," so the game was stopped.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

To make a sandwich, follow the steps. First, put peanut butter on one slice of bread. Next, spread jelly on the other slice. Then press the two slices together.

What should you do right before you press the slices together?
items.answer: Right before pressing the slices together, you spread jelly on the other slice.

steps: Follow the order words: first, next, then.
Before "Then press the two slices together," the step is "Next, spread jelly on the other slice."

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

The pond froze over during the cold week. Because the water turned to solid ice, the ducks could no longer swim there. So they flew to a warmer pond nearby.

WHY did the ducks fly to a warmer pond?
items.answer: The ducks flew to a warmer pond because their pond froze into solid ice, so they could no longer swim there.

steps: Look for the cause words: because and so.
The water "turned to solid ice," so the ducks "could no longer swim there."
That is why they flew away.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A caterpillar becomes a moth in stages. First, the caterpillar spins silk around itself to make a cocoon. Then it rests inside the cocoon while its body slowly changes. Finally, after some time, a moth breaks out and spreads its wings.

Describe the sequence: what happens first, next, and last?
items.answer: First, the caterpillar spins silk to make a cocoon. Next, it rests inside while its body changes. Last, a moth breaks out and spreads its wings.

steps: Follow the order words: first, then, finally.
First it makes a cocoon.
Then it rests and changes, and last a moth breaks out.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

A new dam was built across the river. Because the dam blocked the fish from swimming upstream, fewer fish could reach the place where they lay their eggs. As a result, the number of fish dropped. So workers built a special set of steps called a fish ladder, and the fish could climb past the dam again.

Describe the chain of cause and effect from the dam to the fish ladder.
items.answer: The dam blocked the fish from swimming upstream, so fewer fish reached the place where they lay eggs. As a result, the number of fish dropped. Because of that, workers built a fish ladder so the fish could climb past the dam again.

steps: Start with the first cause: the dam blocked the fish.
So fewer fish reached their egg-laying place, and their numbers dropped.
As a result, workers built a fish ladder to fix the problem.
